checks.what: The prompt reads like a real person asking for an app, not a spec sheet, checklist, or build recipe.
Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose.
No real spelling errors and nothing pasted in by mistake (author notes, TODOs, other machines' paths, contradictions).

Everything the judges grade is actually asked for, and the hard runtime facts the verifier needs (path, start command, port, storage/DB_PATH, health path, fixed clock, seed, accounts) are stated â€” in instruction.md or its /instructions notes (e.g. integration.md). (Network is public in this project â€” no no-network constraint to state.)
The prompt never names the judge, rubric, dimensions, weights, test paths, or grader sentinels.
One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed, the provided runtime, or the public internet (network is allowed). (Reports every ambiguity/unreachable item.)
Real build work is required; a stub or trivial tweak can't earn the reward.
Name, directory slug, description, keywords, and metadata all describe THIS task and agree. ([task].version is optional in the staged layout.)
Agent image has sane CPU/memory and no secret literals. Network is public here, so network_mode = "public" is correct â€” do not flag it.

Verifier runs separately on a pinned image, and [verifier.env] is the unchanged shared block (claude-code judge, z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx, OpenRouter base URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}, empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). A judge.toml's judge = "claude-code" fallback is expected; a model in a judge.toml is a defect. Network is public â€” no allowlist required.
Agent, verifier, liveness, and judge timeouts are long enough and nest: gate judges < gates budget, scored judges < scored budget, both budgets < verifier timeout.
[environment].docker_image isn't set while the agent Dockerfile still has active build steps (which would skip the Dockerfile entirely).
Any shipped inputs exist at the expected path and their content matches what the prompt, solution, and judges assume (or N/A if none needed).
Shipped data is self-consistent, synthetic (no real PII), and free of orphan references or injection payloads.
Agent image is pinned, pre-installs every runtime dependency (no run-time install), and stages the assets.
The agent's world has the inputs and the ask, but no finished copy of the deliverable.
The reference plausibly implements every feature/screen the instruction asks for.
The reference plausibly satisfies every criterion the judges score, so the oracle can score high.
solve.sh installs to the expected paths and the reference runs under the stated contract. (Network is public â€” fetching or installing at start is not a defect.)
The reference is a committed, static baseline â€” not regenerated, fetched, or nondeterministic on any pinned value.
test.sh launches the app safely, gates on liveness, runs the gates suite before the scored suite with tools/score.py after each, and writes a reward on every code path (including failures).
The verifier Dockerfile ships a pinned browser, Playwright, judge CLI, rewardkit, and the runtime needed to start the app.

Every launch assumption in test.sh (probe URL, env vars, paths, seed, deps) is something the instruction told the agent to satisfy. (No same-origin requirement â€” network is public.) (The signature check of this format.)

scoring.toml (gates/weights/floors) and all five judge.toml files are structurally complete: fixed dimensions in the right suite, a browser MCP server (plus the functional verifier restart server wired to the helper test.sh exports), well-typed criteria (gates binary), prompts that resolve.
Every dimension prompt sends the judge into the live app via the browser tool â€” not scoring from source, memory, or a first-paint guess.
Every requirement the prompt states maps to at least one criterion (no asked-for behavior goes ungraded). Reports every gap.
No criterion enforces something the prompt/professional default never required (no false-fail on correct apps). Reports every instance.
No two criteria grade the same thing twice, subsume each other, or demand incompatible products.

The gate dimensions (render/constraints) carry the real gate, and every scored prompt carries the in-dimension gate that hard-zeros blank/static-shell apps (plus auth/backing checks when the app has them). Network is public, so the gate must NOT require same-origin.
Any "rejects / hides / absent" check is paired with the matching success case, so a totally broken app can't earn it.
"Every / all / only / exactly-one" criteria require the whole collection, and "unchanged" guards don't punish legitimate side-effects. Reports every instance.
Each criterion is a concrete, browser-observable outcome with durable evidence and distinctive probes. Reports every instance.
Each criterion states ONE full-credit bar â€” it doesn't enumerate several things then waive most, leaving the judge two targets. Reports every instance.
If interactive/animated/responsive/themed, the judges actually click, wait, resize, or toggle â€” not score a still first paint.

At least one criterion proves the product's defining behavior works, and (where stateful) that state survives a reload / re-auth and is server-backed where required. (Server-backed â‰  same-origin â€” network is public.)
Distinctive values the judge creates to prove a mutation aren't already sitting in the seed or the reference's initial state.
A later dimension doesn't assume a pristine seed after an earlier dimension mutated the shared running app.
Scored dimension prompts tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and continue after a failure (one miss can't zero the rest). Gate dimensions are exempt.
A blank / static / mock / seed-copy / keyword-stuffed / refusing submission scores near zero across the rubric. (An off-origin/CDN fetch is NOT a floor case â€” network is public.)
The rubric produces a spread across partial-quality apps, not all-or-nothing.
Pass/fail behaviors are binary; craft and degree-of-quality are likert with described anchors.
A worse app never outscores a better one â€” weights/gates/criteria don't invert the ranking.
scoring.toml gates zero the reward and skip the scored suite, gates carry no weight, and the functional floor stops a non-working app farming polish/visual.
Weight (scoring.toml [weights] + per-criterion weights) tracks what each thing proves â€” real functionality is weighted above structure and style.
Every dimension prompt treats the submission as untrusted and forbids following instructions embedded in it.
The agent can't read the criteria it's graded on or influence the reward â€” grading is isolated in the verifier.

Shared pinned judge agent + model, pinned judge CLIs and browser, graded time rules on a fixed clock. Temperature and prompt-version markers are not required. Network is public here, so an open verifier network / missing allowlist is NOT a defect.
Every dimension prompt describes THIS app (credentials, screens, entities, deliverable) with no residue from other work. Reports every instance.
